utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Ceko. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall first ask you to give the Court your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I am Stipo Ceko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Secondly, I should also like to ask you to, after you hear my question, wait a little before you answer so that the interpreters can have time to interpret our exchange into the other official languages of the Court, and I shall also wait after I have heard your answer. Very well. So Witness Ceko, let us just quickly go through your particulars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall ask my learned friend, if he objects to leading questions on any of the points, to tell us in advance, but I think I can go -- I can lead the witness through this introductory part, as has already become the custom here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were born on the 4th of October, 1952 in Kruscica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are married and father of three?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I have come from the secondary vocational school in applied chemistry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you matriculate?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you complete your secondary education?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I completed my secondary education in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any rank?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. I did not get any rank. I was a private.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, in 1992 and 1993, in other words, during the war, or rather wars in Bosnia, you held different posts, but basically you were an officer responsible for logistics, first for the Municipal Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, after the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was formed, you had the same job?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the same job for the Stjepan Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, when the Vitez Brigade was formed, you were again in the same job?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, when the war ended, you went on working for the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was established then?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what rank did you acquire in the army of the Federation?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I acquired the rank of a Major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you retired recently?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Or to be more precise, in 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, since we are talking about ranks, during the HVO, that is, in 1992 and 1993, the HVO did not use ranks for its officers, did it.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. It did not use them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were only the posts, the functions, that is, office responsible for this or for that, office of such-and-such, and so on, but there were no ranks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, is it true that you have been Mr. Cerkez's neighbour since 1967?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know him well?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever work with him?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I worked in the same company with him, but we were not employed in the same jobs, but the same company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And that company was the SPS, was it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the largest employer in Vitez, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you remember, very roughly speaking, how large was the staff of the SPS, the Vitezit? How many people worked there?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At the peak of its activity, I believe there were some 3.000 people in the SPS compound, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the ethnic composition of the employees, I presume, reflected the population structure.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One cannot say that any ethnic group was represented in any other way in the SPS?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness Ceko, before the war, did Mario Cerkez, what we are talking about, at that time, did Mario Cerkez also have friends and acquaintances among Croats or among the Muslims too?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez socialised with all the citizens in the municipality of Vitez, equally with Serbs and Muslims and Croats; with everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you yourself were one of his friends, weren't you, and you had common friends too, didn't you? Does that also mean you?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness Ceko, do you remember, in 1992 [as interpreted], when contributions -- when funds were -- in 1990 when the funds were raised amongst the citizens there for the building of the mosque, do you remember that? And could you -- would you say that it was in the latter half and towards the end of 1990, on various occasions?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly, but yes, I do think that it was roughly that time, 1989, perhaps 1990, 1991. I can't really remember, but that was roughly at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you, as a citizen of that place, contribute for the mosque too?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, I did not, because at that time I was rather bad off financially. But I know that my father, yes, contributed to help the construction of the mosque in Kruscica, and I know very many other people from Vitez who also donated some money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and your father are homesteaders there; you've lived there for a very long time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so did Mario Cerkez and his father, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. And I also think that he also donated some money for the construction of the mosque in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard about that?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever see the document, some receipt for the money?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I saw it, my father's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. That is, that he gave the money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I should like now to introduce a document, because I want the witness to confirm the contents of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, when this document reaches you eventually, will you please tell us, is that the receipt for those donations that I asked you about a while ago? Could we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be marked D92/2.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could this document, based on what we talked about, confirm what we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Those were the receipts that people were issued when they would donate money for the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can put it aside. Witness Ceko, Mario Cerkez was mentioned on the eve of the war, or rather, the disintegration of Yugoslavia. Did, at that time, Mario Cerkez show any interest in the political life, in political developments or participation in the political life?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At that time, precisely, Mario Cerkez showed no signs of being interested in political developments because at that time, those national parties began to emerge. As far as I know, however, he was never a member of a party not -- nor did we ever go to any of their conventions. He simply -- I think once we went somewhere, but he wasn't simply interested in politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when those national parties began to emerge in 1990, 1991, there were some conferences, some conventions all the time, weren't there, almost on a daily basis, all the time; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that it was only once that you attended, you and Mario together attended such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then basically, had he attended more of such meetings, you would have known about that?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know if Mario Cerkez was a member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Mario was not a member of the HDZ. I know that in 1991, 1992, 1993 that during all those years, he was not a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Is it correct that to you and other friends, Mario Cerkez began to say that as far as he could see the pre-war developments, that sooner or later there would be an armed attempt by the army of Yugoslavia to prevent the disintegration of Yugoslavia and try to keep Bosnia by force, by weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. There must be a limit as to how much we can get the impressions of one man out of the mouth of another. That was a leading question about what was in the state of mind of someone else. I'll try not to make any further objections because I know the difficulties that Mr. Kovacic has, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Once we get to controversial matters, just deal with the matter neutrally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I was just expecting whether my colleague will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, don't -- try, yourself, Mr. Kovacic, to find a way to organise the matter and organise yourself. Once we start getting towards matters of dealing with the war then, on the whole, then they may well be controversial such as this one.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Should I answer this question or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it. What was Mario's attitude to and his view as to what could be expected during those days on the eve of the breakout of the war?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez, who followed the developments in Croatia, thought -- realised what might happen, and we often talked and he told me that an open aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina was very likely with a view to keep him -- Bosnia-Herzegovina within Yugoslavia. And he even told me on that occasion it will reach us no doubt, and we shall have to organise ourselves somehow, our villages, our areas, our families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you agree with that at that time or later on perhaps?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, yes, in principle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that same time, 1990, 1991, is it fair to say that economic problems in your environment began?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: True. In 1991, following the aggression on Croatia, there was also some economic troubles that found the reflection in Bosnia-Herzegovina, more precisely our company, the SPS. There was a shortage of raw materials, we could not collect the money that were due us, there were no funds. So that the volume of production began to decline from one day to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it at that time that some people were suspended, were laid off temporarily?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I was laid off for some five or six months, but repeatedly depending on the amount of work that there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Mario Cerkez was ever laid off temporarily?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Perhaps even more than I was. I wouldn't know exactly but yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was the chief criterion of the employer, that is, the factory, for laying off people?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The criterion was the work place, the job, that is the requirements of that particular job only, exclusively, nothing else. That is, if there was work, then one went on working. Where there was no work and where the volume of production had dropped, people were simply temporarily sent home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- would you say that the ethnicity of workers was one of the criteria to lay off people?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. No. That was not it. Out of the question. It really depended only and exclusively on the requirements of the job. All -- people of all ethnicities were laid off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this document distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, I will ask you now to read this certificate, who issued it, why, and then I'll have two questions to ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please just tell me the name of the company Vitezit-Cromem, what is that company?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Vitezit-Cromen Ltd. was the successor to the SPS because it changed its name and became this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here, we have a different -- four different periods of time during which, according to this certificate, Mario Cerkez was temporarily laid off. Do you find it acceptable regarding the time? Of course, I know you can't give us exactly to a day, but would that be the period of time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I even thought that there were longer periods when he was at home waiting to be called back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. Can I have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be D93/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in early 1993, Cerkez was planning to get -- a wedding?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What wedding was it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It was the church wedding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Cerkez already married in a civil ceremony?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Cerkez had contracted a civil marriage some 10 or 12 years before that. That is, at any rate, he got married before me and he was living with his wife, Slavica, and her two children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you do not know why did he decide to also undergo a church ceremony?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I think I do know reasons too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see, you do. Will you tell us?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: In May, 1993, there was to be the Holy Communion. It is the ritual with us, the Catholics, and the children began to talk about it and I think it was at the urging of children that they wanted to receive their -- their First Communion, and because they could not do that unless their parents had been wed in the church, I think that was the reason why he decided to do that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know what date was fixed for the wedding?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which was the date?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It was the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I think it was to take place in late afternoon. Around 5.00 or 6.00 is when these ceremonies were held. That was the time for both baptisms and weddings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the wedding take place?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, why not.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, we came from work, because we were next-door neighbours. And we had just arrived home in order to have a shower and change and get ready for the wedding. But when we arrived home, his wife, Slavica, said that the Commander of the Operative Zone had been asking for him and wanted him to call him immediately. So naturally, I went back into my house. I had a shower and dressed and got ready. But Mario never came back. And sometime in the evening or in late afternoon, a summons came to me, or rather I was being called. The wife told me that the Commander was phoning to tell me that they had to report to the command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, in view of the next day and the events that ensued, could you perhaps remember when you were told that the wedding had been postponed? Who told you that, and can you remember any of these details?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I do not know that the wedding was delayed, because when I returned home -- and I came home after midnight, after 12.00, so the wedding simply could not take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But you told us that you had got ready, you came home, dressed up. Was it your wife who came to tell you that you were not going to do that, or was it Cerkez who came to tell you that the wedding was off, that you would not be going to the church?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you are positive that the wedding ceremony did not take place?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Oh, yes, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I should now like to produce another document, and I should like to invite the witness to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Kovacic. I'm following the transcript. I'd like to ask a question of the witness. You were supposed to attend the wedding, if I understood him right. That was on the 15th of April, 1993. He went home. I failed to understand how it came about -- I'd like to know who gave him a call, who phoned him that day -- I think it was at the end of the afternoon -- who rang him up to tell him that, according to the transcript -- [In English] "They had to report to the command of the brigade. The wife told me that the Commander was phoning to tell me..." [Interpretation] So whose wife is mentioned here? Could you give us some more details on what happened that night, that evening? Thank you, Mr. Ceko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Please tell us about this in detail now.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: On the 15th of April we worked, as usual, at headquarters until about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. We went home together, both I and Mario Cerkez. On the way, we took our time. I think we arrived home only around 4.00. Since we live right next door, since we are next-door neighbours, when we got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mention -- you mean Mario Cerkez? So when you say that you live next door, you mean his house and your house are close to one another?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you came back from work about the same time as he did, around 4.00; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, precisely at the same time. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Then when we arrived in the yard in front of the house, Slavica, the wife of Mario Cerkez, went out and said that he should report immediately to the Operative Zone, that Blaskic was looking for him. And he returned immediately and I stayed at home. I waited at home. I took a shower, I changed, and I was waiting for Mario to come back home as well so that we could go to the church for the wedding. However, Mario did not return at all. And I was also called up from the command of the Viteska Brigade. I was called from home to go to the command of the Viteska Brigade, which is what I did. And I did not return until midnight that night, that is, midnight between the 15th and the 16th. So due to that fact, we could not go to attend the wedding. That is how I know that the wedding did not take place on that day, although it had been scheduled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell the Chamber why you were rung up urgently to report to the brigade command that night? Why did they call you as a matter of urgency and why did you stay until midnight on that night?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I know why they called me from brigade headquarters. Mario told the officer on duty in the brigade to get all the members of the command to the brigade together so that they could wait there at the brigade command. That is why I was called into the brigade command. That is to say, that Mr. Mario Cerkez called the duty officer to tell him to get all the members of the brigade command together so that they would wait for him. And that is why I was called, because I was a member of the brigade command as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... that you met together with Mario Cerkez on that night?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. We met with Mario Cerkez that same night. I think it was around 2100 hours, 2130. Mario Cerkez came to the brigade command and we held a short briefing then. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do. But you have to tell us what the briefing was about.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. At that meeting, Mario Cerkez told us that an order would arrive from the of the Operative Zone, that we would have to be combat ready, because there has been some information that on the next day there could be an attack of the BH army on the municipality of Vitez. Also at that brief meeting I found out that the attack could possibly take place from Kruscica and Vranjska -- that was the estimate -- towards the centre of Vitez. I also know that our task was -- that is, the task of the Viteska Brigade at that time -- to try to stop the BH army from passing, that is to say, to blockade the roads from Kruscica and Vranjska towards Vitez. So that was our task. And I know that he entrusted Anto Bertovic with this -- at the time he was Commander of the battalion we had in the brigade at the time -- to get all these people together, to inform all the people he could get in touch with, and that they should report and try to blockade those roads: Kruscica, Vranjska, towards Vitez. That was our assignment. After that, Mario Cerkez went someplace, I don't know where, and I did not see him again until the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell the Chamber, provided you know about it, what Cerkez did between the time when you left him at 4.00 in the afternoon and the time of the meeting, later on?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you please repeat your question, because I did not manage to register everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... came home together -- it was 4.00 -- that Mr. Cerkez's wife told him that he had to call urgently Mr. Blaskic. Then you went to the headquarters of the brigade, I suppose in Vitez, and you said that you met with Cerkez at 9.00 in the evening. Do you know what he did between 4.00 in the afternoon and 9.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know whether he was at the headquarters of the brigade in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think he was at the command of the Operative Zone. I don't know about the command of the brigade in Vitez. Nobody said that to me and I didn't ask. When I arrived, he was not there. And also he was not there, as I told you, until about 2100 hours. I don't know exactly. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The command of the Operative Zone, what does that mean? Where is it located?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The Commander of the Operative Zone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the command, about the headquarters there where Mr. Blaskic was.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The command was at the Vitez Hotel, right next door to the building where the brigade headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Mr. Blaskic was at the headquarters of the command on that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At whose command? Of the brigade or the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: He was probably at the command of the Operative Zone. I don't know. I think he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we could complete one question here and then go back to our chronological order, as I had planned originally. Do you know whether that night Cerkez returned home at all or not? Was he at home that night or not?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It is only in the morning, on the 16th, at 5.00 in the morning, that I saw his car in front of the house, when I went back to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do not know when he came during the night?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned to the command in the morning, did Cerkez come before you or after you?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: After me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you perhaps tell us roughly whether he came a few minutes after you, half an hour after you? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was about an hour later. I can't remember exactly, but perhaps around 6.00; that's when he came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So until that time, in the meantime, until he came, and after you had left, Cerkez was obviously at home; right?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, I believe he was at home, because when I left, his car was in front of his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not see him?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. I only saw his car in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now let us complete this particular line of questioning so that we don't have to go back. Cerkez's house, where you live, is this near the zone that you mentioned precisely, that is, the road between Kruscica and town?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Cerkez's house and my house are in the immediate vicinity, that is to say, on the very border between Vitez and Kruscica, so that is to say, in the immediate vicinity of the area where this attack on Vitez was expected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to where we had stopped earlier. I would like to have a document -- oh, it has been distributed. Witness Ceko, please take a look at this document. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I have not seen this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did have the opportunity of --

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Seeing such documents?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the stamp on page 2, the big one, multicoloured. Is this the stamp of your municipal parish office?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: This is the stamp of the parish in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the parish office?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, of the parish office of the church that is in Stari Vitez, Sveti Juri, St. Juri.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the spring of 1992, in Vitez, did political parties talk about possible joint organisation of the defence of your area against Serbs?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, they did. It was in early 1992. It could have been April or May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Go on.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, they tried to reach an understanding to set up a joint brigade, a Muslim/Croat Brigade, I mean, to have it organised so that it could organise the defence of the municipality of Vitez against the aggression of the JNA and the ARS. However, it never came true. At that time, it was offered to me to organise one of the logistical duties in that -- well, let's call it brigade which I had accepted in principle. However, it was never operationalised, that is, the joint Brigade was never formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that this initiative waxed and waned and that it lasted for sometime?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. People would say, "yes, let's do it," and then it will grind to a halt and then once again, people start talking about it but it never came true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were even some preparations taken, you told us some posts were offered?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Certain posts were mentioned in the brigade that I was offered, for instance, a post in the logistics and I had accepted it. And there were already some discussions about the name of the brigade and that for a while, HMVO was the topical name, that is, Croat Muslim Defence Council, but I think this was not accepted by the representatives of the SDA and there were some other difficulties. There were also attempts to print some membership cards for that brigade because people thought that it was about to be formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us, please, you -- you were using the term the 1st Vitez Brigade; is that it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, at least that was at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that had it been formed, that is what it would have been called?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, yes, we talked about the 1st Vitez Brigade, HMVO, and there were different proposals on the table, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Witness Ceko, could you now explain in a few words, what were village guards?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Village guards, that was -- well, it was the armed people, people arm, themselves, their own initiative and guarded their villages against gangs and whatever else might come. They organised themselves. They would elect their commander amongst themselves. They stood guard and protected their villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when did this self-organisation in the villages began?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, it began, I think, already in late 1991 and went on in 1992. Late 1991 or beginning of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where you lived in the northern part of Kruscica, close to Rijeka, were there any village guards there?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those guards monoethnic, were they mixed, did they take shifts or not?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, since I live in Kruscica, of course, I know best the situation in Kruscica. In Kruscica, there were both monoethnic and mixed guards, Croats and Muslims, since Kruscica is the largest village in the municipality. There are several hamlets next to the village of Kruscica, and they were simply Croat hamlets and there they would have purely Croat guards. And on top of Kruscica near to the fish pond, there were mixed guards, that is both Croats and Muslims. And the hamlet above Rijeka, to the left of Rijeka, Baresine Kuce is what we call it, they also had mixed guards made of Croats, Muslims and Romanie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any authority, be it civilian or military, in 1992 or until the conflict in April 1993 run or control the village guards? Did any authority control those village guards?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. No. Because in 1991, people began to arm themselves and to organise themselves. At that time, that was not a lawful activity so that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the time when the JNA still functioned?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the JNA still functioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think we can move on to another topic. What was the Municipal HVO Staff in your municipality, in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The municipal government organised a Municipal Staff. That was a body, a civilian body, the task of which was to organise the defence against the Serb aggression, that is, against the JNA and the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time when you -- I apologise, we forgot to do this. When, to the best of your recollection, did the -- was it begun to organise the Municipal Staff?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I don't know. April, May, it could have been, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us if, at that time -- could you now go back into the past and tell us if the central government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was operational?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, it was not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The state had already begun to fall apart and so that the government did not function, that is, one could feel there were problems in every day life?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the activities that you talked about regarding the task of the Staff, at about what time did the Staff organise the first armed groups which then participated in certain activities against the ARS? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, that was roughly at about that time. I know there was an action of some ten men who volunteered and went to Slimena. That action was led personally by Mario Cerkez and Colonel Filipovic, that is, they brought together a group of volunteers from Vitez and went to there to take over the depot from the JNA, and I believe it was on the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the 3rd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Cerkez headed a group of volunteers from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the group comprise Croats only?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At that time, no, it wasn't only Croats. There were also some Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that action was not conducted only by the group from Vitez, it was a coordinated action involving several municipalities -- several places in the municipality and several groups of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It was a joint action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you remember if that Vitez group had also a crew, a Muslim crew of an anti-aircraft gun and that there were Muslims from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And who was the Chief of the Staff when it was formed?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: You mean the Municipal Staff in Vitez? The Commander of the Municipal Staff was Marijan Skopljak from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us until when was Marijan Skopljak the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Marijan Skopljak remained the Chief of Staff until about the end of 1992, perhaps -- November, perhaps, because it was at that time that the defence office attached to the HVO government was formed. And with some other members of the Staff, he then moved over to the defence office and some other members of the Staff had stayed behind in the Staff, but it had already fallen apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, tell us, please, is it true that in the early days of the Staff, you and Mario were, by and large, responsible for the logistics?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: From the very beginning of the Staff, Mario Cerkez was mostly responsible for those matters and I helped him. But after a short while, I took over the logistics from Mario, and Mario was then responsible for operative matters, that is, organisation of groups and so on and so forth, and I took over the logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, can we agree that at the time when the Staff ceased to operate, that is, when the defence office was established and you told us that that was sometime in late November, that at that time, Cerkez had been promoted, I mean conditionally speaking, since there was no official nominations, that he had then become the second highest official in the Staff?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, de facto, Mario Cerkez became the second man, man number two in the Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in the early days, the Staff was in Marijan Skopljak's house. Could you tell us roughly until about when that was the case?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: That was for about a month perhaps. It could have been April. In the beginning in Marijan Skopljak's house or rather in his garage, and then they moved to the Vitez Hotel. It could have been for about a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when Blaskic's Operative Zone came, then you moved from the hotel. When Blaskic's Operative Zone came, then the Municipal Staff was not transferred from the hotel, that is, you stayed in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Oh, yes, we stayed in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registry please help me to show the 66/2, D66/2. Could the witness be shown it? It's a photograph. Could we have it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, will you please look at this house and tell us if you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose is it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: This is Marijan Skopljak's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us which part of the house housed the Staff? Use the pointer, please, to indicate where was the Staff.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Just a moment. So it was in this auxiliary building, yes, the -- in the upper door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will you tell us, what is this black part, this dark part in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: You mean in front of the house, what is it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, this is kind of a porch and this is where the restaurant was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The restaurant?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it also belonged to Marijan Skopljak, did it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it all belonged to Marijan Skopljak and this thing over here is the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But since we are looking at photographs of houses, perhaps we should also clarify another thing. I should like to produce another exhibit and ask the witness to tell us if he can identify this house.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D95/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, will you please have a good look either on the ELMO or in front of you, wherever you can see it better, and tell us if you can identify it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, this is Mario Cerkez's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any -- do you have any doubt about that?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you contribute to the building of this house, personally? Did you invest your work into this house?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Kovacic. When was the house built?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: This -- the construction of the house began, I think, in 1985 or thereabouts, 1984, 1985 perhaps. I'm not sure. It could be plus or minus two years. I don't even know when I began to build my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You contributed to the building of the house as what, in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I wasn't really building it, but since we are next-door neighbours, then it is a custom with us to help one another. So I often helped him when he built it and, of course, he had some masons, but he, himself, did most of the work and his father and his father-in-law and I only helped him from time to time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps just one question to explain. Was it a custom in your area when somebody builds a house that you invite an entrepreneur to do it, that is, you entrust the whole business to a company or to build it yourself with the help of friends and relatives, and perhaps a professional builder now and then?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, the custom with us is to build the house yourself with friends, to organise work jointly because nobody had enough money, nobody could afford a company to hire a company or an entrepreneur. We would only perhaps hire a mason or a carpenter, but otherwise we'd do it ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In September/October 1992, did the Main Staff form units to go to fight and defend Jajce against the aggression of the ARS and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. In September/October 1992, the Municipal Staff also sent shifts to Jajce to try to defend it against the JNA and the ARS at that time. The Muslims and Croats were putting up joint defence at that time in Jajce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you remember if -- do you remember, perhaps, how many men to a shift there were? What was the maximum number?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, it would be about the strength of two platoons, about 60 men or something. As many as one could gather at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You remember that on the 19th of October, 1992, the BH army blocked the road through the Lasva Valley in the Vitez municipality at two places?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that these roadblocks prevented the departure of the HVO members from the Busovaca/Kiseljak in the direction of Jajce?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The barricades, that is, the passage was prohibited at two places near Bila and Bilovit [phoen] and they wanted to prevent the passage. That is, a shift from Busovaca/Kiseljak was to go up there, but they set up barricades and one could not get through. I wasn't at the roadblock in Ahmici, but on the 19th I personally went to collect our comrades in Bila, to go to -- to collect bread --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... to collect bread from Bila because that is where it was baked for us, but I couldn't get through and that is how I learned that the roadblocks had been set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We have in the transcript "comrades" instead of "bread." The witness said that he was going in Bila to pick up bread, not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think he said, initially, he said he was going to pick up comrades or something of the sort.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's mistake. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It was bread. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you saw for yourself that the road had been blocked there near Ahmici next to the Catholic cemetery?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, I did not see it there. I saw it in Bila, not down there. I did not see about the one down there, but I heard that it had also been set in front of Ahmici, and I saw the second one up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And afterwards did you hear about the one that you saw near Bila? And that was next to the Bosna construction company, was it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear afterwards, either that same day or at any time, that that roadblock had been removed of their own free will, that Franjo Nakic managed to prevail in the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that Mr. Franjo Nakic and others negotiated with Muslims. And the one which was in Bila, next to Bosna, as you say, was removed subsequently as a result of those negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But I'm asking you about this event, because the Court has heard a great deal about this. Where did you have the materiel depot at the time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At the time, the materiel depot of the Vitez Municipal Staff was in Kruscica, next to the Lovac Motel. That was a building near Lovac Motel, the Sumadija company. That is where the Staff had its depot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Ceko, Kruscica is predominantly a Muslim village, is it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And especially in that part, in that part where the motel is and where the fish pond is. And in October 1992 the Municipal Staff continued to hold -- to keep a depot in a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were responsible, you were in charge of that depot, were you?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that situation, because you had the road blocked, you had your depot in the middle, in the heart of a Muslim village, did it -- were you concerned about this?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, because on the 19th, the roadblock in Bila was removed, but the other one below Ahmici remained. And after negotiations, after several rounds of negotiations -- or at least that's what I heard -- with representatives of the SDA, that is, Muslims, to remove the barricade. However, on the 19th the roadblock was not removed, and I was really worried about this, because the depot was in Kruscica. Because all that day, that is, the 19th of October, we could not reach an understanding. I was afraid that I would lose that depot there, because in the Kruscica school there was a unit of the BH army, and that was a company, I should say, of about a hundred men or so. And I was afraid that I might be conflict and that I would lose my materiel. So I suggested to the Commander, that is, the Chief of Staff, Marijan Skopljak, to try and pull out the materiel from the Kruscica depot. And he said, "We'll see." And after that, that is, perhaps two or three hours later, Mario Cerkez called and said that he would try to organise the salvage of the materiel from up there. And that's how it was. In the evening, Anto Bertovic called and said that he was calling to see to resolve the matter. Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it would be best if you told us the whole story.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Anto came and he said that he was in charge of the attempt to get this ammunition out, and I said, "No problem. I am ready to come with you." And he came with a group of soldiers. I think that, by and large, those were men from the military police. So we went to Kruscica, to the depot. We somehow made our way there. And we loaded the ammunition, because that was the most important thing at the time. Two smallish lorries. One was a small TAM and the other I think TAM 110. And we loaded them with ammunition. And because we could not pass through Kruscica, we started from Kruscica towards Plavac Motel, that is, by the summer cottage in the locality of Bistro, by the Plavac Motel, to Zabrdze, in order to go around Kruscica and reach Vitez. However, on our way to Plavac Motel, we came across an ambush laid by a small group of ABiH soldiers, and there there was an exchange of fire. So the action was led by Anto Bertovic and there was an exchange of fire. We lost two soldiers that night. But we nevertheless made it through that place and brought the ammunition and stored it in the warehouse which is next to the Vitez municipal hall. Anto Bertovic was slightly wounded on that occasion, one man was captured, and the other one turned up in the morning, so that we learned that he had simply lost his way as he fled. So we pulled out those two lorries --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. It's very difficult to follow all this detail. I'm not sure that it's really necessary. Do I understand the position right that in Kruscica, the Municipal Staff had its headquarters at Marijan Skopljak's house and also had a depot in which there was ammunition and other equipment? Is that the position? It should be made clear, then. It's not clear. As I understand it, what the witness is saying is he's trying to remove the ammunition from the Kruscica depot because of the incidents on the 19th. But we hadn't heard of the depot before. It suddenly emerged in the evidence. Perhaps you could clear it up, shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ceko, may I? Mr. Ceko, I'm going to put questions to you, step by step. Since when have you had this logistics base in Kruscica? When was it first established?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The logistics base in Kruscica was established at the beginning of the month of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away is it, approximately, of course, from the house of Pero Skopljak -- sorry, Marijan Skopljak? At that time your headquarters was there; right?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It is three kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the best would be if I ask for D85/2 to be shown. That's one of the maps that we were using yesterday. Perhaps the witness can show where the house of Mr. Marijan Skopljak is and where this logistics base was. Could the video director please zoom in on Kruscica? Could we see the town of Vitez more, the lower part of the map, towards the south. Perhaps it would be a good thing to move the camera lower, please, or perhaps the usher can help us with this. This is good. This is fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ceko, please show the road that you lived on.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It is this road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, so that's the road that goes south to Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the witness at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show the house of Mario Cerkez, the one that you showed on the photograph a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again the interpreter does not hear the witness's answers at all.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: From the main crossroads, it is about 400 metres towards Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your warehouse at the motel that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We can leave the map all together now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's variously been called a warehouse, a depot, a base. Is it all the same place?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but that is how they call it, so I'm using their terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sure you are. It's very confusing. If we can stick to one term, it would be easier. And do I understand that it was in the motel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Remind me of the name, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I intervene? This was not at the motel. This was a facility next door to the Lovac Motel. It was a log cabin. It was the warehouse of the Sumadija company from Kruscica that was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just by the motel?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, just by the motel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we call this "the depot by the motel," is that a clear term?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The depot where you unloaded the materiel that you brought into town, can you explain where that is?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, the depot where we brought the ammunition is three metres away from the building of the municipality of Vitez, just by the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the very centre of town, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. For the second time now during your testimony you have mentioned, just now, Mr. Anto Bertovic. Perhaps we should not leave any doubts there. Do you think Anto Bertovic is an honest man?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that he is a good and able soldier?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I also agree that he is a good and able soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you find out and what did you find out about the elimination of the roadblock near the village of Ahmici by the Catholic cemetery?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: You mean what I found out or when I found it out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What and when.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I found out on the 20th of August that there was an armed conflict at the roadblock and that the roadblock was removed. I also found out that a soldier from Kiseljak got killed and also a young man from Ahmici was killed. That's what I heard through hearsay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you yourself, you were not there, nearby?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any group under the control of the HVO Staff in Vitez that was involved in this action?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Trial Chamber for their permission to move into private session for a few minutes, please. We need to mention the name of a person whose name should not be mentioned in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person that we just identified now as AS, was this person involved in any way? Did you see that person the night when you were bringing the ammunition from the depot up there into town?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. I do not remember having seen that person at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that person otherwise?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know him?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: I know him. I know him. He's my neighbour. He lives in the neighbouring village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he lives near you?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, he lives about two kilometres away, as the crow flies, from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please: Did you ever, at any time, not only within this time frame that we are discussing now, were you ever together with Mario Cerkez, your assistant Mimo, and this person that we are mentioning? At any point in time were you together with these people that you can mention that? Were you all together at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. We were not together at any point in time, all this group together: I, Mimo, Mario Cerkez, Mlakic, and the person that you call AS. We were never together, the four of us, at a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take care of that all together. During the war, did you ever hear Cerkez mention any threatening or derogatory terms as far as Bosniak Muslims are concerned?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, never. I never heard Cerkez speak that way. I never heard any swear words or any threats addressed to Muslims. No, that was never the case. No. Cerkez is a serious man. Not even during the most intensive conflicts, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we can move out of private session now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are out of private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Ceko, can you tell us when the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The Brigade Stjepan Tomasevic was established at the beginning of December 1993 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that approximately -- or rather a bit earlier, the defence department was established because the HVO Staff had practically stopped to operate, and you who were on the Staff were told that now a new brigade would be established soon?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that soon a new brigade was to be established. All of us who stayed in the Municipal Staff in order to prepare the organisation of shifts, indeed, on the 1st of December, I think it was, we went to Novi Travnik, and about seven or eight of us -- it was about seven or eight of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: So we from the Staff, and perhaps somebody else, we went at the beginning of December. Perhaps it was the 1st of December. We went to Novi Travnik, and that is where the command post of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was, at the hotel, at the new hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just correct the transcript. Page 37, line 14. You were talking about the beginning of 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, indeed, at the beginning of December, you were sent to this brigade. Where was its seat?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Its seat was in the new hotel in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was never in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: It was never in Vitez. The headquarters of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was never in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were ever any such plans to have it in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the first Commander of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The Commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was Borivoje Malbasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was his deputy?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: His deputy was Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What post did he hold?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was Malbasic reassigned to another post?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993, Borivoje Malbasic was sent to another post and Mario Cerkez was appointed acting Commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, witness: This word that you keep using, "deputy commander," we've heard it a few times.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Well, that is the acting commander, the person who acts as the commander of the Brigade, so in fact, it is the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this acting -- this word "acting commander," it implies a temporary nature, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there is no doubt that Cerkez was then Commander?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. For us, he was the top man then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the only task of the brigade at that time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At that time the only task of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was to consolidate the defence line above Novi Travnik -- Slatka Voda, Mravinjac, Kamenjas, Vucja Glava -- against the JNA and the ARS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember at least some colleagues who were members of the command of this brigade in addition to you and Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please name those who you remember.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: In addition to Mario and myself, in the command of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade there was Zeljko Sajevic, Rudo Kurevija, Borislav Jozic, Ivo Sucic, Drago Damjenovic, Jozo Zuljevic, Srecko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That is sufficient. Witness Ceko, is it correct that in December 1992 and in January 1993, while Malbasic was Commander, that Mario Cerkez was considerably involved in the way in which the municipalities would finance this?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. When the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established, when Borivoje Malbasic was Commander, Mario's first and primary task was to organise the system of financing, that is to say, to organise the support of the municipalities of Vitez and Novi Travnik. I think he did this very well, because this municipal support did start to function, from both municipalities. He did that quite well. Before that, these relations were impaired. This was not his only task. His task number two was to improve the quality of the defence line. That is to say that emphasis was laid on the engineering aspect of the defence line against the ARS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ceko, as far as this improvement of the quality of the defence lines against the ARS is concerned, who was Cerkez's chief helper?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who worked with Cerkez, for the most part, on this engineering enhancement of the defence line?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: In addition to Cerkez, the command consisted half of people from Vitez and half from Novi Travnik. So there was Sabljic, Zeljko from Novi Travnik and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And others. And this Sabljic, is that the same person who was commander after Cerkez left, or rather after all of you went from Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. At that time he was chief of engineering in the command of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade. But then, since the brigade then split into two parts, then he became Commander of this brigade of Stjepan Tomasevic that remained in Novi Travnik. Sabljic Zeljko; I'm talking about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I think this would be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ceko, let us continue. Will you tell us, please, you were, as you told us, in Novi Travnik at the time when you were a member of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade command and Cerkez was there at the same time. That is quite clear. Just now tell me this: Between December 1992, that is, from the time that you came to Novi Travnik until March 1993 while you were with the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, was there, in the town, in Novi Travnik or in its immediate environs, was there any significant conflicts between people, between Muslims and Croats? I'm not asking you about the troops, I'm asking about citizens. Were there any conflicts between peoples?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Between December 1992 until March 1993, there were now [as interpreted] serious conflicts between Muslims and Croats. There were incidents here and there at the expense of both peoples, that is, perpetrated against one another but those were minor incidents, but there were not any serious conflicts and especially there were no conflicts between the HVO and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite sure that on no occasion, while you were there, was there a confrontation between the HVO, between HVO units and any units of the ABiH, I mean as formal and official units of the either of the two armies?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you remember, when was the initiative launched to -- of the municipal government in Vitez to form a municipal brigade which, later on, became known as the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that initiative to form a separate brigade, that is, the Vitez Brigade by the municipal council in Vitez. That was in early March 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if, at that time, in early March until middle of March, Cerkez conducted preparations for the formation of the brigade or -- did you take a part in that?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember until the middle of March 1993, certain preparations were already underway to form the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, did you consider the options for the headquarters of the command?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it was already decided by that time, or rather when the name for the brigade was chosen, that that was the Vitez Brigade. And at that time also, the command place for the brigade was identified, and that was the Workers' University in Vitez. So those were the preparations at the time. And names of people who were -- joined the command were already on the table, were already discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that pursuant to Blaskic's command of the 24th of April, 1993, that Mario Cerkez was appointed the Commander of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. There was the order in writing by Blaskic whereby Mario Cerkez was appointed the Commander of the Vitez Brigade on the 24th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that order at that time?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I showed it when we discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I don't think there is any need to produce that document. It was here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that point in time, that is, as of that order onward, did Mario Cerkez and his associates begin to systematically organise the command of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, Cerkez was involved in the organisation of the command of the brigade itself, that is, accommodation and establishment of various services of the brigade. Because at that time, we were already moving because the Staff moved from the Workers' University, they went elsewhere, and we moved into those premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you mentioned the battalion, the only unit under the command of the brigade command at that time in those early days of the brigade was which one?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: At that time, when the Vitez Brigade was formed, the only unit was this battalion which had formerly been a part of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and that was the only unit of the Vitez Brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander of that battalion was?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Anto Bertovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that battalion have some facilities where soldiers were quartered all the time, I mean barracks?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The battalion in the Vitez Brigade did not have any barracks where men would be accommodated all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it did not have any facilities of the kind. So how did the battalion form the units which it needed at various times for individual tasks?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: The battalion engaged men by summons, that is, it had a list of some 300 men. That is how strong it was at the time. So it would summon men, and shifts would be formed and they would go to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did members of the brigade who would be called up, did they use the term "active duty formation"?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They would call it active duty formation. That was the expression they used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this term, did it refer to the fact that somebody was on the list from which men were called up?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those summons that you mentioned, were they always in writing?

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
utterances.text: No. Sometimes there will be some in writing, but the men would be called orally too because they were all volunteers. They were all volunteers, and they would respond to either oral or written summons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if a certain military conscript from that list or from some other list that existed in the defence department or if -- because defence office also had a list, and if somebody was summoned and would not respond using whatever excuse, did he suffer any consequences for that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: STIPO CEKO
